# laya-scraper

> An AI writes the scraper once, plain code runs it after that. Give it a website and one line of plain English and it returns a validated table of every item on that site's listing.

The LLM is used only to build a recipe for a site: the listing URL, the paging
strategy and one proven selector per field. Runs after that make no LLM calls,
so they cost nothing and return the same answers each time.

Measured on ukri.org: the build took 25 LLM calls, 133,779 tokens in and 24,211
out, $0.069 at MiniMax-M3 prices, 7.7 minutes for 100 items. Every run after
that: 0 calls, $0, 78 seconds.

Five targets tested at 100 items each, precision then recall:
patents.justia.com 100/94, ukri.org 97/91, odi.org 96/90, gov.uk 100/77,
catalog.data.gov 96/70. Low recall is fields left blank and marked unreliable
rather than guessed.

- Page: https://laya.vibe-coding.fans/
- Source, MIT: https://github.com/qxZap/laya-scraper
- Built on laya by NandhaKishorM, a small non-generative decision model.
